articles.title_en: The White House restores media access after court order.
articles.title_ru: Белый дом восстанавливает доступ СМИ после судебного приказа.
articles.preview_en: The White House allowed CNN, Politico and MS NOW back into its press facilities following a federal judge’s directive.
articles.preview_ru: Белый дом разрешил крупным американским новостным организациям вернуться в прессцентр после судебного приказа.
articles.full_en: The White House’s decision to reopen its press briefing room has drawn international attention. The White House permitted CNN, Politico and MS NOW to re‑enter the building after a federal judge ordered the reversal of earlier bans. The bans had been imposed in 2020 when the Trump administration barred several outlets for alleged bias. The reversal underscores the judiciary’s role in safeguarding press freedom in the United States. Global watchdogs have praised the move as a reinforcement of democratic norms that affect allied nations. The restored access enables journalists to report directly from the executive branch, improving transparency for foreign audiences. The episode reminds world leaders that legal checks can curb executive overreach in media matters.
articles.full_ru: Белый дом принял решение открыть прессцентр, что вызвало интерес международного сообщества. Белый дом разрешил крупным американским новостным организациям вновь войти в здание после судебного приказа об отмене прежних запретов. Запреты были введены в 2020 году администрацией Трампа изза подозрений в предвзятости. Отмена ограничений подчёркивает важность судебного контроля над свободой прессы в США. Международные правозащитные организации охарактеризовали шаг как укрепление демократических принципов, влияющих на союзные государства. Восстановленный доступ позволяет журналистам напрямую сообщать из исполнительной власти, повышая прозрачность для зарубежных аудиторий. Эпизод напоминает мировым лидерам, что правовые механизмы способны ограничивать произвол власти в вопросах медиа.
articles.meta_en: The White House reinstates access for major news outlets after a judge’s order, highlighting judicial protection of press freedom.

articles.preview_ru: Wallace Collection, London The British sculptor’s delicate, intimate and ready-to-pop creations feel right at home among Hertford House’s rococo masterpieces Maybe it was that wine glass I broke this
articles.full_en: Wallace Collection, London The British sculptor’s delicate, intimate and ready-to-pop creations feel right at home among Hertford House’s rococo masterpieces Maybe it was that wine glass I broke this morning while unloading the dishwasher, but seeing a Rachel Kneebone porcelain sculpture suspended makes me nervous. Can those skinny wires really hold the weight? Should there perhaps be a soft landing just in case? Emerging from a tangled clump of ribbons and roses are a couple of bone-white bubbles, ready to pop. This is art that quite literally hangs in the balance; a sense of peril is what makes it so marvellous. Born in 1973, the British sculptor is the latest contemporary artist to be invited to show her work at the Wallace Collection. Following in the footsteps of Damien Hirst, Flora Yukhnovich and Grayson Perry, Kneebone has positioned nine milky sculptures made between 2017 and 2026 throughout Hertford House.
